subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging IGCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for IGCSE Maths simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

learningObjectives.title: Mean from frequency and grouped data
Scatter diagrams, correlation and line of best fit

questions.q: For the data set 4, 7, 9, 9, 12, what is the median?
questions.explain: With 5 values already in order, the median is the middle (3rd) value, which is 9.

questions.q: Find the range of the data: 15, 3, 8, 21, 6.
questions.explain: Range = largest - smallest = 21 - 3 = 18.

questions.q: The mean of five numbers is 12. Four of the numbers are 8, 10, 14 and 16. What is the fifth number?
questions.explain: Total = mean x count = 12 x 5 = 60. The four known numbers sum to 48, so the fifth is 60 - 48 = 12.

questions.q: Which average is unaffected by one very large outlier value in a data set?
questions.explain: The median is the middle value once ordered, so a single extreme outlier does not shift it, unlike the mean.

questions.q: A frequency table shows: value 2 (frequency 3), value 5 (frequency 4), value 8 (frequency 3). What is the mean?
questions.explain: Sum = 2x3 + 5x4 + 8x3 = 6 + 20 + 24 = 50. Total frequency = 10, so mean = 50 / 10 = 5.

questions.q: For grouped data, an estimate of the mean uses which value from each class?
questions.explain: Because exact values are unknown, you multiply each class midpoint by its frequency, then divide by the total frequency.

questions.q: Grouped data: 0<x<=10 (frequency 2, midpoint 5) and 10<x<=20 (frequency 3, midpoint 15). Estimate the mean.
Why is a mean from grouped data called an 'estimate'?
options: Because midpoints are used instead of the exact original values
Because grouped data has no mean
questions.explain: Grouping loses the exact values, so using class midpoints only approximates the true mean.

questions.q: In a pie chart of 40 people, one sector represents 10 people. What angle does that sector have?
On a pictogram, one symbol represents 8 cars. How many symbols are needed to show 20 cars?
questions.explain: 20 / 8 = 2.5, so you draw two full symbols and one half symbol.

questions.q: Which chart is best for comparing the frequencies of separate, discrete categories?
questions.explain: A bar chart uses bars with gaps to compare discrete categories; histograms are for continuous grouped data.

questions.q: A histogram class has frequency 24 and class width 8. What is the frequency density?
questions.explain: Frequency density = frequency / class width = 24 / 8 = 3.

questions.q: On a histogram a bar has frequency density 2.5 and class width 6. What is the frequency for that class?
questions.explain: Frequency = frequency density x class width = 2.5 x 6 = 15. On a histogram the area of the bar equals the frequency.

questions.q: In a correctly drawn histogram, what does the AREA of each bar represent?
questions.explain: Because height is frequency density (frequency / width), area = density x width = frequency.

questions.q: When plotting a cumulative frequency curve, each point is plotted at which x-value of the class?
questions.explain: Cumulative frequency counts everything up to and including the class, so points are plotted at each class upper boundary.

questions.q: A cumulative frequency curve is drawn for 60 students. At which cumulative frequency do you read off the lower quartile?
questions.explain: The lower quartile is at n/4 = 60/4 = 15 on the cumulative frequency axis.

questions.q: For 80 values, the lower quartile read from the curve is 42 and the upper quartile is 58. What is the interquartile range?
questions.explain: IQR = upper quartile - lower quartile = 58 - 42 = 16.

questions.q: A scatter diagram shows points falling as you move right, close to a straight line. What correlation is this?
questions.explain: As one variable increases the other decreases (a downward trend), and points near a line means the correlation is strong negative.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a line of best fit on a scatter diagram?
options: To model the trend and estimate values
questions.explain: The line of best fit summarises the trend, letting you estimate one variable from the other by reading off the line.

questions.q: In a stem-and-leaf diagram the stem is '3' and a leaf is '7', where the key is 3 | 7 = 37. What value does this represent?
questions.explain: The stem gives the tens digit and the leaf the units digit, so 3 | 7 reads as 37.
